question.problem: The root of the function $f(x)=-\sqrt{8-2x}+4$ is $x=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
-\sqrt{8-2x}+4=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{8-2x}+4 & =0 \\ -\sqrt{8-2x} & =-4 \\ \sqrt{8-2x} & =4 \\ (\sqrt{8-2x})^{2} & ={4}^{2} \\ 8-2x & =16 \\ -2x & =8 \\ x & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{8-2(-4)}+4 & =0 \\ -\sqrt{8+8}+4 & =0 \\ -\sqrt{16}+4 & =0 \\ -4+4 & =0 \\ -4+4 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=-4.$
